title: Earth: Our Shared Home

standard_text: Earth as a shared home for plants, animals and people; interdependence, producers, consumers and decomposers; food chains; threats to the environment and endangered animals; people and movements that protect nature; eco-friendly habits and the 3 Rs (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 10).

key_big: All living things share one Earth.
key_sub: Plants, animals and people depend on each other.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth is the shared home of all living things, and they depend on each other. Green plants are producers that make food from sunlight; animals are consumers; decomposers such as mushrooms and bacteria break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil. A food chain shows who eats whom, for example grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle.

Cutting forests, pollution and hunting put many animals in danger. People have protected nature through the Chipko movement, the Bishnoi community and Project Tiger. We can help with eco-friendly habits: reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and plant trees.

Example

In grass → deer → tiger, the deer eats…

follow the arrow

Answer: grass

Example

A mushroom is a…

breaks down dead things

Answer: decomposer

Common mistakes

  • Reading food chain arrows the wrong way.
  • Thinking decomposers are harmful.
  • Thinking one person cannot make a difference.
